subject: HealthSync — buying path alignment, procurement & hosting questions
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthSync — buying path alignment, procurement & hosting questions

Hi Lauren — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map next steps internally and with procurement: 

Recap (super short):
- Demo covered Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated/reserved pools; showed cost/latency tradeoffs for 2 candidate models.
- HealthSync use case: live patient-message summarization + search; expected 6M tokens/month at pilot.

Asks / decision inputs we need from your side:
1) Economic buyer / sign-off: who owns the P&L or who signs the reserved capacity contract? (Name + best email)
2) Procurement/legal gating: do you have a standard intake form or PO process? Any mandatory clauses (DPA, data residency)?
3) Security requirements: you mentioned SOC 2 — do you need Redwood to complete a security questionnaire or upload artifacts?
4) Latency & SLA targets: do you have a p95 token latency target or an error/SLO bar for production?
5) Preferred hosting: are you leaning Hosted (fastest onboarding) vs Dedicated (predictable throughput) vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for initial pilot?

I attached a short MAPP (market-app-playbook) and a draft SOW that outlines typical Dedicated timelines — these are just to speed alignment (HealthSync_Redwood_MAPP.pdf, SOW-draft-v0.1.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm 1–5 above, we’ll map a short mutual action plan and route any procurement docs to your team.
- If it helps, Ben can run a quick perf sketch vs your sample payload next week.

Thanks — appreciate the time.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.g@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: HealthSync_Redwood_MAPP.pdf (summary), SOW-draft-v0.1.pdf (draft)

From: Lauren Gibbons <lauren.g@healthsync.com>

Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSync — buying path alignment, procurement & hosting questions

Hi Sean — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and looping in procurement.

1) Economic buyer: Mark Reynolds (CFO) will sign commercial commitments. I copied him separately to introduce.
2) Procurement: we have a standard intake form and PO flow; procurement@healthsync.com owns it. They typically run legal review + DPA/ indemnity checks. Timeline depends on contract size — for pilots we can do a lighter flow but still need a DPA.
3) Security: SOC 2 Type II is required for production. For pilots we accept a security questionnaire; procurement can share the template.
4) Latency/SLA: For patient-facing summarization we want p95 inference under ~200ms ideally, p95 under 300ms as acceptable for pilot. Error rate / availability target is 99.5% for pilot.
5) Hosting: leaning toward Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable performance, but open to Hosted if we need to move faster for the pilot.

Procurement will send the intake form; Mark will be the economic buyer but I’ll be the day-to-day sponsor.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Gibbons
Director of Product, HealthSync
lauren.g@healthsync.com | +1 (415) 555-2244

Thanks Lauren — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups to make sure our internal recommendation aligns with HealthSync priorities: 

- Economic buyer / procurement path: we’ll request a short intro to Mark and procurement to map commercial cadence. Can you confirm Mark's email or should we coordinate through you?

- Latency detail: you mentioned p95 ~200ms (preferred) / 300ms acceptable. To size Dedicated pools we need: average request token length and a 99th percentile concurrency estimate during peak hours (or an example QPS). If you don’t have exact numbers, a proxy (e.g., 12 req/s peak, avg 120 tokens/request) will do.

- Deployment suggestion: because predictability is important and you're leaning Dedicated, our usual playbook is: pilot on a small Dedicated pool (pin a model variant) + fallback to Hosted for overflow. That gives predictable p95 + fast recovery during spikes. We can document that in the MAPP.

- Security artifacts: Ben will follow up to collect any questionnaire. We can provide SOC 2 artifacts under NDA or via Procurements portal.

- Budget check: can you share a target monthly spend band for pilot so we can size the proposal (e.g., $15k–$40k/mo)? If you prefer not to share numbers, we’ll propose 2 sizing options.

I attached an updated MAPP that highlights the pilot deployment pattern and a proposed mutual action plan. I’ll hold on drafting a commercial until we get a sense of budget and Mark's involvement.

Thanks — Sean

Hi Sean — apologies for the delay. Procurement attached the intake form and flagged the initial timeline. Key updates below: 

- Economic buyer confirmed: Mark Reynolds (CFO) — mark.reynolds@healthsync.com (cc'd). He wants a short 1-page summary of the pilot objective and expected spend before formal sign-off.
- Procurement timeline: intake + legal review generally completes in ~4–6 weeks for pilots; if terms are within standard DPA and liability bands they move faster. Target for contract execution: end of August.
- Security: procurement asked for SOC 2 Type II report and standard security questionnaire (attached). They prefer artifact exchange via the procurement portal link above.
- Latency / deployment: Confirmed target p95 <= 200ms preferred; 300ms tolerated during heavy loads. For pilot they will start with Dedicated reserve if Redwood provides clear autoscale/fallback policies.
- Budget: Finance has approved an initial pilot budget in the $20k–$35k/month band; final number dependent on committed throughput and model choice.

Next steps suggested by HealthSync:
1) Sean / Redwood to provide a 1-page pilot summary + proposed pilot SOW (cost ranges for two sizing options) for Mark.
2) Ben to pick up security questionnaire exchange with procurement and deliver SOC 2 artifacts.
3) Sean to propose a mutual action plan with dates targeting contract execution by end of Aug.

We attached: procurement-intake-form.xlsx and HealthSync_security_questionnaire.pdf.

Thanks — Lauren
